How a harbour keeps its tide

Article masthead: the pond in March.
Masthead navigation: sections of the pond.

A harbour mill holds the tide behind a gate and spends it through a wheel. The pond fills on the rise, the gate shuts at the turn, and the wheel runs until the basin is back to the level of the sea outside it.

Article header: the pond in April.

Families who lived beside the pond learned to read the water the way other people read a clock, and the hours of work drifted forward by about fifty minutes every day.

There is only a gate, a pond, and a wheel, arranged so that the ocean does the lifting and the miller does the waiting. Steam did not care about the moon, and most of the mills went quiet once it arrived.
